fixes.explanation: Nice guess, since gold is what most of us think of when we hear "giving to a king." But David doesn't mention gold or silver anywhere here. He says, "Ascribe to the LORD, O heavenly beings, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength." (Psalm 29:1) Glory and strength are what he calls on them to ascribe to Him, and you can't pack those in a cookie box.

Yes, baker. "The LORD sits enthroned over the flood…" (Psalm 29:10) A flood is a scary thing, and I think David wants us to notice where the LORD sits in relation to it. Then he adds, "the LORD is enthroned as King forever." (Psalm 29:10) Flood on one side, a King on His throne forever on the other.

Shur is a real wilderness in the Bible (Exodus 15:22), so you know your deserts, and that's not nothing. But David names a different one here: "the LORD shakes the Wilderness of Kadesh." (Psalm 29:8) I know, desert names run together like dough in a hot oven. Hold onto Kadesh for this verse, friend.
